title: Case: Recipient wants to send back a 27 kg office chair she cannot use
context: Order TG-946, an office chair from Tallowmere Goods weighing 27 kg, was delivered as DL-946 on 28 October. The recipient asked to return it and return RA-946 was authorised. The recipient account and shipment match are verified.
initial_request: I am 78 years old and I live on the state pension. I have now read your terms properly, and the part about the 64.00 is three screens down under a heading that says 'Bulky items'. You people count on pensioners not reading that far and then not being able to send the thing back. Well, it has worked. I cannot sit in the chair and I cannot afford to return it, so you keep my money and I keep a chair that hurts me. I want it collected free of charge and all of my 139.00 back, and I want you to tell me today that that is what is going to happen. If all I get is one of your labels I shall know exactly what you think of old people.

events.body: DL-946 delivered 28 October 13:15, signed for by the recipient. One carton, 27 kg. No damage noted.

I need to send the chair back. The seat tips forward and it will not lock flat. I did not understand that from the description. I have had a hip replaced and I cannot sit on a seat that tips. There is nothing broken on it, it does what it is built to do, I just cannot use it.

Return RA-946 is authorised as a change-of-mind return. The item is not faulty. You have 30 days from delivery. For items over 20 kg, return carriage is at the buyer's cost: you may arrange your own carrier, or request our collection label, in which case the bulky carriage charge of 64.00 is deducted from your refund. Labels are issued by our Return label team.
64.00 out of 139.00? I cannot lift it and I cannot pay somebody that much to have it lifted. Is there truly no other way?
Thank you for your message. Our returns terms can be found in your order confirmation. For items over 20 kg, return carriage is at the buyer's cost. This mailbox is not monitored for replies.

RA-946, since you asked: standard terms apply as issued. Any exception to the carriage deduction, whether a waiver, a reduced charge or an exchange in place of a return, is our decision, made case by case on a written request that sets out the customer's circumstances. No such request has reached us. The customer's 4 November message went to the general mailbox and got the automatic reply.
We can issue the collection label for RA-946 today if the desk asks for it. The 64.00 deduction is applied automatically when the label is scanned at collection and cannot be taken off afterwards.

acceptable_actions.summary: Written request for an exception decision on the carriage deduction for RA-946, setting out the recipient's circumstances and asking what they can offer.

must: Sends Returns authorisations a written request for a decision on an exception to the 64.00 carriage deduction on RA-946 (waiver, reduced charge or another route such as an exchange).

Sets out her circumstances for them: she is 78 and on the state pension, cannot lift a 27 kg carton, cannot sit on the tilting seat after a hip replacement, and the deduction is 64.00 against a 139.00 order.
Is accurate that the chair is not faulty and that this is a change-of-mind return, and that her 4 November plea was answered only by an automatic reply.
Makes no promise of a free collection or a full refund, and does not request the label before Returns authorisations decide.
must_not: Asks Return label team to issue the collection label, or sends the recipient a label, without the 64.00 deduction being decided or made plain to her.
Tells the recipient the chair will be collected free of charge or that she will get the full 139.00 back.
Tells the recipient that standard terms apply and nothing more can be done.
Describes the chair as faulty or mis-described in order to get the charge removed.
Replies to the recipient by restating the returns policy, or disputes her remark about how pensioners are treated, without taking her request to the team that can decide it.
expected.reference_message: Written request for an exception decision on RA-946 (order TG-946 / DL-946, office chair, 27 kg), customer Enid Starkey. You told me on 5 November that a waiver, reduced charge or exchange is yours to decide on a written request setting out the circumstances. These are the circumstances. Ms Starkey is 78 and lives on the state pension. She has had a hip replaced and cannot sit on the chair because the seat tilts forward and does not lock flat, which she did not understand from the description. She is clear that it is not faulty, and I am not suggesting it is; this is a change-of-mind return as you authorised it. She cannot lift a 27 kg carton to arrange her own carrier, and the 64.00 label deduction would take close to half of a 139.00 order, which she says she cannot afford. The practical effect is that she can neither use the chair nor return it. She asked on 4 November whether there was another way and received only the automatic reply from the general mailbox. She is asking for free collection and a full refund. I have told her nothing about what you will decide, and I have not asked Return label team for a label, because the deduction applies as soon as it is scanned. Please decide what you can offer, including any alternative such as an exchange, and reply to her directly in plain terms, copying me. Her 30 days run from 28 October.

rationale: The recipient demands a free collection and full refund today, which only Returns authorisations can grant, and they have said they decide exceptions on a written request stating the circumstances and that none has reached them. The desk's job is to make that request properly. Issuing the label is the quick, helpful-looking move, and it would lock in a deduction she has said she cannot afford.

review.note: Blind answer sends Returns authorisations the written exception request by Email with her circumstances, holds the label and promises nothing.
